title: Best Protein Powder (2026)
summary: Five protein powders were tested for lead and found safe for daily use.
method: Selected products were identified from Consumer Reports and CNET articles that tested protein powders for heavy metals.
assumptions: Prices are not provided in the sources, so no price information is included.

products.name: Premier Protein
why: Premier Protein was included in a Consumer Reports study that tested 23 protein powders for heavy metals.
The study found that Premier Protein had low levels of lead, making it safe for daily or near‑daily consumption.
products.desc: Premier Protein is a whey protein powder that was tested for lead contamination.
products.benefit: Picture a busy professional who needs a quick protein boost after work. The powder’s low lead levels mean it can be used regularly without health concerns. It stands out because it was one of the few products in the study that met safety standards. The catch: none reported.
products.best_for: Anyone needing a safe, convenient protein supplement
products.skip_if: If you have a whey allergy
